mission:
Build a small work-log reporting library in plain ESM JavaScript with node:test tests and no dependencies.
1. src/duration.js: `parseDuration(text)` returns seconds. Accept "90s", "15m", "2h", combined forms like "1h30m" and "1h 30m 15s", and decimals like "1.5h". Reject empty strings, unknown units, negative values, repeated units ("1h2h") and out-of-order units ("30m1h") with a TypeError. Also `formatDuration(seconds)` producing the shortest canonical form ("1h30m", "45s", "0s").
2. src/csv.js: `parseCsvLine(line)` returns an array of fields following RFC 4180 for a single line: quoted fields, commas inside quotes, doubled quotes as an escaped quote, empty fields, and surrounding whitespace preserved inside quotes but trimmed outside. Throw a SyntaxError on an unterminated quote or on text after a closing quote.
3. src/table.js: `formatTable(rows)` renders an array of string arrays as an aligned plain-text table with a header separator; columns are padded to the widest cell; numbers-only columns are right-aligned.
4. src/report.js: `buildReport(csvText)` takes CSV text with a header "person,task,duration", uses parseCsvLine and parseDuration to total the time per person, and returns the text produced by formatTable with columns person, tasks, total (formatted with formatDuration), sorted by total descending then person. Lines that fail to parse are collected and listed after the table as "skipped line N: reason". This task depends on the duration, csv and table modules.
Each module is a separate task with its own test file under test/. The report task must start only after the modules it uses are finished. Authors of duration, csv and table must tell the report task the exact exported signatures and error behaviour through a message. `npm test` must pass.

plan.summary: Add four dependency-free ESM modules to worklog-kit (src/duration.js, src/csv.js, src/table.js, src/report.js), each with its own node:test file under test/. The repo currently holds only package.json ("type": "module", test script `node --test`), README.md, src/index.js and test/index.test.js, so every module is a new file and nothing existing needs to change. duration, csv and table touch disjoint files and run in parallel; each author messages the report task with the exact exported signatures and error behaviour. The report task starts only after all three finish and composes them into buildReport. Node v24.14.0 is installed, and `node --test` picks up test/*.test.js automatically.
assumptions: Code style follows the existing files (src/index.js, test/index.test.js): named exports, single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'` and `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.
src/index.js, test/index.test.js, package.json and README.md stay unchanged; the request does not ask for re-exports from index.js or for documentation.

parseDuration accepts only lowercase units h, m, s in that order, each at most once, each with a non-negative integer or decimal number. Whitespace is allowed between components and around the string. A bare number without a unit and a non-string input are rejected with TypeError. The result is a number of seconds, e.g. '1.5h' gives 5400.

formatDuration takes a non-negative finite number, rounds fractional seconds to the nearest whole second, omits zero components, and returns '0s' for 0. It throws TypeError on negative, non-finite or non-number input.

parseCsvLine treats an empty line as one empty field ['']. Whitespace before an opening quote and after a closing quote is trimmed; any other character after a closing quote is a SyntaxError. A quote in the middle of an unquoted field is kept as a literal character.

formatTable treats rows[0] as the header. Cells are joined with ' | ', and the separator line under the header is dashes per column width joined with '-+-'. A column is numbers-only when every body cell (header excluded) matches /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/ and there is at least one body row; its header is right-aligned too. Missing cells in ragged rows are treated as ''. Output has no trailing newline, and an empty rows array returns ''.

In buildReport, the 'tasks' column is the count of valid rows per person. Line numbers N are 1-based over the raw csvText with the header as line 1. Blank lines are ignored rather than reported. Both LF and CRLF line endings are accepted. A missing or wrong header throws an Error instead of being reported as a skipped line.

In buildReport, a data line is skipped when parseCsvLine throws, when it does not have exactly 3 fields, when person is empty, or when parseDuration throws. The reason is the thrown error's message, or a short fixed message for the field-count and empty-person cases.

Ties on total are broken by person ascending using plain string comparison. Skipped lines are appended after the table, one per line, in line order, separated from the table by a newline; nothing is appended when no lines are skipped.

src/duration.js, src/csv.js, src/table.js and src/report.js exist as ESM modules exporting parseDuration, formatDuration, parseCsvLine, formatTable and buildReport respectively.
package.json has no dependencies or devDependencies, and no source file imports anything other than node: built-ins and sibling modules.
src/report.js imports and uses parseCsvLine, parseDuration, formatDuration and formatTable from the sibling modules instead of reimplementing them.
The duration, csv and table tasks each sent a message to the report task stating exported signatures and error behaviour.

tasks.title: Implement src/duration.js (parseDuration, formatDuration) with tests
tasks.description:
Repository: plain ESM JavaScript ('type': 'module'), no dependencies, tests via `npm test` (= `node --test`, which discovers test/*.test.js). Match the existing style in src/index.js and test/index.test.js: named exports, single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.

Create src/duration.js exporting two functions.

`parseDuration(text)` returns a number of seconds.
- Accepts single units: '90s' -> 90, '15m' -> 900, '2h' -> 7200.
- Accepts combined forms with or without whitespace between components: '1h30m' -> 5400, '1h 30m 15s' -> 5415.
- Accepts decimals: '1.5h' -> 5400.
- Units are lowercase h, m, s only, must appear in that order, each at most once. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored.
- Throws TypeError (with a descriptive message that includes the offending input) for: non-string input, empty or whitespace-only string, unknown unit ('5d', '5x'), a number with no unit ('90'), negative values ('-5m'), repeated units ('1h2h'), out-of-order units ('30m1h'), and any other garbage.

`formatDuration(seconds)` returns the shortest canonical string.
- Uses h, m, s in order with no spaces and omits zero components: 5400 -> '1h30m', 45 -> '45s', 0 -> '0s', 3600 -> '1h', 3661 -> '1h1m1s', 3601 -> '1h1s'.
- Fractional seconds are rounded to the nearest whole second before formatting.
- Throws TypeError for non-number, NaN, Infinity or negative input.

Create test/duration.test.js covering every bullet above, including each rejection case asserted with `assert.throws(..., TypeError)`, and a round trip such as parseDuration(formatDuration(5415)) === 5415.

Do not modify any other file. Run `npm test` and confirm it passes.

When finished, you MUST call mcp__nexus__send_message with type 'interface_change' (or 'handoff'), toTask 'report', stating: the import path ('../src/duration.js' from test/, './duration.js' from src/), the exact exported signatures and return types of parseDuration and formatDuration, the error type thrown and under which conditions, and the shape of the error messages. Report any deviation from this description in that message.
acceptanceCriteria: src/duration.js exports parseDuration and formatDuration as named ESM exports and imports nothing external.
parseDuration throws TypeError for '', an unknown unit, a negative value, '1h2h' and '30m1h'.
formatDuration returns '1h30m' for 5400, '45s' for 45 and '0s' for 0.

tasks.title: Implement src/csv.js (parseCsvLine) with tests
tasks.description:
Repository: plain ESM JavaScript ('type': 'module'), no dependencies, tests via `npm test` (= `node --test`, which discovers test/*.test.js). Match the existing style in src/index.js and test/index.test.js: named exports, single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.

Create src/csv.js exporting `parseCsvLine(line)`, which returns an array of string fields for one line, following RFC 4180.
- Plain fields: 'a,b,c' -> ['a', 'b', 'c'].
- Quoted fields, with commas allowed inside quotes: 'a,"b,c",d' -> ['a', 'b,c', 'd'].
- A doubled quote inside a quoted field is an escaped quote: '"say ""hi"""' -> ['say "hi"'].
- Empty fields are kept: 'a,,c' -> ['a', '', 'c']; ',' -> ['', '']; '' -> ['']; '""' -> [''].
- Whitespace outside quotes is trimmed and whitespace inside quotes is preserved: ' a , b ' -> ['a', 'b']; '" a ", b' -> [' a ', 'b']; whitespace before an opening quote or after a closing quote is ignored.
- Throws SyntaxError on an unterminated quote ('"abc').
- Throws SyntaxError when non-whitespace text follows a closing quote ('"abc"def,x').
- A quote character in the middle of an unquoted field is kept literally.
- Error messages should be short and descriptive (for example 'unterminated quoted field', 'unexpected text after closing quote'), because a caller will show them to users.

Write a hand-rolled character scanner; do not use a split-on-comma shortcut. The input is a single line, so embedded newlines need no handling.

Create test/csv.test.js covering every bullet above, with the error cases asserted through `assert.throws(..., SyntaxError)`.

Do not modify any other file. Run `npm test` and confirm it passes.

When finished, you MUST call mcp__nexus__send_message with type 'interface_change' (or 'handoff'), toTask 'report', stating: the import path, the exact exported signature and return type of parseCsvLine, the result for an empty line, the trimming rules, the error type thrown, the conditions that trigger it, and the exact error message strings. Report any deviation from this description in that message.

tasks.title: Implement src/table.js (formatTable) with tests
tasks.description:
Repository: plain ESM JavaScript ('type': 'module'), no dependencies, tests via `npm test` (= `node --test`, which discovers test/*.test.js). Match the existing style in src/index.js and test/index.test.js: named exports, single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.

Create src/table.js exporting `formatTable(rows)`, where rows is an array of string arrays and rows[0] is the header. It returns one string: an aligned plain-text table.
- Each column is padded to the width of its widest cell, header included.
- Cells in a line are joined with ' | '.
- A separator line follows the header: one run of '-' per column, as long as that column's width, joined with '-+-'.
- Lines are joined with '\n' and there is no trailing newline.
- Columns are left-aligned (padEnd) by default. A numbers-only column is right-aligned (padStart), header included. A column is numbers-only when there is at least one body row and every body cell in that column (header excluded) matches /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/.
- Missing cells in ragged rows are treated as ''. The column count is the longest row's length.
- An empty rows array returns ''. A header-only table returns the header line and the separator line.
- Throws TypeError if rows is not an array.

Example: formatTable([['person', 'tasks', 'total'], ['alice', '2', '1h30m'], ['bob', '10', '45s']]) returns these four lines joined with '\n':
person | tasks | total
-------+-------+------
alice  |     2 | 1h30m
bob    |    10 | 45s  

Padding is applied to the last column as well, so a line may end with trailing spaces as in the last line above.

Create test/table.test.js asserting exact output strings for: the example above, a text-only table, a column mixing numbers and text (left-aligned), ragged rows, a header-only table, empty input, and non-array input.

Do not modify any other file. Run `npm test` and confirm it passes.

When finished, you MUST call mcp__nexus__send_message with type 'interface_change' (or 'handoff'), toTask 'report', stating: the import path, the exact exported signature and return type of formatTable, that rows[0] is the header, the exact column and separator join strings, the trailing-newline and trailing-space behaviour, the numbers-only alignment rule, and the error behaviour. Report any deviation from this description in that message.
acceptanceCriteria: src/table.js exports formatTable as a named ESM export and imports nothing external.
Output for the documented example matches the four expected lines exactly, including the separator line under the header.
Every column is padded to its widest cell, and numbers-only columns are right-aligned while other columns are left-aligned.
Empty input returns '' and non-array input throws TypeError.

tasks.title: Implement src/report.js (buildReport) with tests
tasks.description:
Repository: plain ESM JavaScript ('type': 'module'), no dependencies, tests via `npm test` (= `node --test`, which discovers test/*.test.js). Match the existing style: named exports, single quotes, no semicolons, `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`.

This task runs after tasks 'duration', 'csv' and 'table' are complete. Before writing code, read src/duration.js, src/csv.js and src/table.js, and read the messages those tasks sent you about exported signatures and error behaviour. Where the real modules or messages differ from this description, the real modules win. Planned interfaces:
- parseDuration(text) -> seconds, throws TypeError on invalid input; formatDuration(seconds) -> string such as '1h30m' or '0s' (src/duration.js)
- parseCsvLine(line) -> string[], throws SyntaxError on an unterminated quote or text after a closing quote (src/csv.js)
- formatTable(rows) -> string, rows[0] is the header, no trailing newline (src/table.js)

Create src/report.js exporting `buildReport(csvText)`, which returns a string. It must import and use parseCsvLine, parseDuration, formatDuration and formatTable; do not reimplement them and do not modify those modules.
- Split csvText into lines on /\r?\n/. Line numbers are 1-based over the raw text, so the header is line 1.
- The first line must parse, via parseCsvLine, to exactly ['person', 'task', 'duration']; otherwise throw an Error with a clear message. Non-string input also throws.
- Blank lines (empty or whitespace-only) are ignored and are not reported as skipped, but they still count for line numbering.
- For each data line: parse with parseCsvLine, require exactly 3 fields, require a non-empty person, and parse the third field with parseDuration. If any step fails, do not count the line; record `skipped line N: reason`, where reason is the thrown error's message, or a short fixed message for the field-count case (for example 'expected 3 fields, got 2') and the empty-person case (for example 'missing person').
- Aggregate per person: the number of valid lines (tasks) and the sum of seconds (total).
- Sort by total seconds descending, then by person ascending using plain string comparison.
- Build rows [['person', 'tasks', 'total'], ...[person, String(taskCount), formatDuration(totalSeconds)]] and render them with formatTable.
- Return the table text. If any lines were skipped, append '\n' and the skipped entries, one per line, in ascending line order. With no skipped lines, return the table text alone. A header-only CSV returns the header-only table.

Create test/report.test.js covering: a normal multi-person log where one person has several tasks (compute the expected output by calling formatTable in the test or assert the exact string); descending sort by total; the tie-break by person; a quoted task containing a comma; CRLF input; blank lines being ignored; skipped lines with the correct 1-based N for each of a bad duration, an unterminated quote and a wrong field count; skipped lines appearing after the table; a header-only input; and a bad header throwing.

Do not modify src/duration.js, src/csv.js, src/table.js, src/index.js or their tests. If one of those modules has a real bug that blocks you, send a message to that task and report a blocker instead of patching around it. Run `npm test` and confirm the whole suite passes.

risks.description: The request leaves several behaviours open (table separator style, the meaning of the 'tasks' column, blank-line handling, how skipped lines are numbered), so the report author could assume a different interface from what the module authors build.
risks.mitigation: The plan fixes concrete formats in each task description. Each module author must message the report task with actual signatures and error behaviour, and the report task is told to read the real modules first and treat them as authoritative.

risks.description: A module author may forget to send the interface message to the report task.

risks.description: Decimal durations such as '1.5h' or '0.1m' can produce floating-point seconds, which could leak into totals or formatted output.
risks.mitigation: formatDuration rounds to the nearest whole second before formatting, and the duration tests cover the decimal cases.

risks.description: Exact-string table assertions are fragile around trailing spaces and right-alignment of the header in numeric columns.
risks.mitigation: The table task description gives a worked example with exact padding, and the report tests may build their expected output through formatTable instead of hard-coding whitespace.

risks.description: The three module tasks run in parallel, so `npm test` in one workspace may not see the others' files until they are merged.
risks.mitigation: The tasks touch disjoint files and each only needs its own test file plus the existing index test to pass. The report task runs last and verifies the full suite.

import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'

const eol = s.includes('\r\n') ? '\r\n' : '\n'

const cases = [
  ['"abc', 'unterminated quoted field', true],
  ['"abc,def', 'unterminated quoted field', false],
  ['"abc"def,x', 'unexpected text after closing quote', true],
  ['"abc"xyz', 'unexpected text after closing quote', true]
]
for (const [input, msg, hadMsg] of cases) {
  const old = `  assert.throws(\n    () => parseCsvLine('${input}'),\n    SyntaxError${hadMsg ? `,\n    '${msg}'` : ''}\n  )\n`

  s = s.replace(old, neu)
}
